# Tim Lytle

> Engineering leader and backend architect with 20+ years building API-first systems, and a conference speaker on APIs, testing, Docker and engineering culture. Available for consulting, advisory work, and the right longer-term role.

Tim has given 26 conference talks (51 deliveries) since 2012, mostly at PHP and developer conferences. Ratings and attendee comments are public on joind.in.

## Pages

- [Home](https://timlytle.net/): what Tim does, recent talks, and how to get in touch
- [Talks](https://timlytle.net/talks.html): every talk, where it was given, slides and ratings

## Talks

- [BattleSnake Hackathon](https://timlytle.net/talks/battlesnake-hackathon.html): The tutorial slot for the php[tek] BattleSnake tournament: quickstart, docs overview, and a dissection of a snake.
- [Event Sourcing Teardown: Understanding the Pattern](https://timlytle.net/talks/event-sourcing-teardown-understanding-pattern.html): Events, aggregates, projections, snapshots, and commands, taken apart so the pattern is easier to use well.
- [Is This Test Worth It? Evaluating the Real Value of Testing](https://timlytle.net/talks/is-this-test-worth-it-evaluating-real-value-testing.html): Unit, integration, contract, or end-to-end: the question that matters is what a test actually buys you.
- [Let Go of Ownership](https://timlytle.net/talks/let-go-ownership.html): A keynote on swapping the ownership model for stewardship: in code, career, and community.
- [Yak Free Docker: Everyday Uses That Aren't Deployment](https://timlytle.net/talks/yak-free-docker.html): Docker for the everyday stuff that is not deployment: runtimes, dev tools, and throwaway utilities.
- [You Can Handle APIs: Introducing API Handler](https://timlytle.net/talks/you-can-handle-apis-introducing-api-handler.html): A no-slides, just-code introduction to API Handler, a PSR-15 middleware pattern for building APIs.
- [HTTP Tortilla: Make PSR-7 Burritos](https://timlytle.net/talks/http-tortilla-make-psr-7-burritos.html): Wrapping PSR-7 request and response objects so the framework pieces you already use fit together.
- [HAL It Works](https://timlytle.net/talks/hal-it-works.html): How a production API team uses HAL as a hypermedia format, the constraints on it, and the client-side cache pattern it enables.
- [HTTP Patterns: PSR 7 & 15 By Example](https://timlytle.net/talks/http-patterns-psr-7-15-by-example.html): A hands-on look at HTTP Messages and HTTP Handlers and how to properly leverage them.
- [Building First Class Client Libraries](https://timlytle.net/talks/building-first-class-client-libraries.html): Do consistent API patterns and good HTTP clients make the API-specific client library obsolete?
- [Hypermedia Without The Hype](https://timlytle.net/talks/hypermedia-without-hype.html): Hypermedia and HATEOAS without the skynet: applying what works for human navigation of the web to APIs.
- [Patterns For API Development](https://timlytle.net/talks/patterns-for-api-development.html): Common code patterns used when building APIs with PHP, with examples.
- [Versioning: Every Way Is Wrong](https://timlytle.net/talks/versioning-every-way-is-wrong.html): API versioning: you do not want to do it, and when you do, someone will say you did it wrong.
- [URIs – The Path To Your APIs](https://timlytle.net/talks/uris-path-to-your-apis.html): URIs are the path to your API data, and different design patterns use them very differently.
- [API Request & Response Formats](https://timlytle.net/talks/api-request-response-formats.html): Requests and responses are the core of an API. Pick formats that are natural for the consumer.
- [Authentication: The Token API Talk](https://timlytle.net/talks/authentication-token-api-talk.html): How to authenticate API users, when you do not need to, and what each method trades off.
- [APIs Are Everywhere](https://timlytle.net/talks/apis-are-everywhere.html): We consume APIs every day as SDKs and libraries. The same design principles apply to the web APIs we build.
- [Yak Free API Tips & Tricks You Can Use Right Now](https://timlytle.net/talks/yak-free-api-tips.html): API tools, services, and techniques that need little or no setup and that you can use before I stop talking.
- [Birds of a Feather: API Design](https://timlytle.net/talks/birds-feather-api-design.html): A roundtable on API development and API design.
- [Hands-On API Design](https://timlytle.net/talks/hands-on-api-design.html): A workshop on going from an API-first decision to an API people actually want to use.
- [Building PHP Daemons & Long Running Processes](https://timlytle.net/talks/building-php-daemons-long-running-processes.html): Stop abusing cron. Daemonize a PHP script that responds responsibly to process signals.
- [Adventures of a Contract Developer](https://timlytle.net/talks/adventures-contract-developer.html): A contract developer for ten years shares a philosophy of contracting and the clients you will run into.
- [Robust Second-factor Authentication with PHP](https://timlytle.net/talks/second-factor-auth.html): Single-use codes, phone verification, apps, and physical devices: how each second factor works and what it costs you.
- [The API Toolbox](https://timlytle.net/talks/api-toolbox.html): The tools worth having around when you build and consume APIs.
- [The Wonderful World of APIs](https://timlytle.net/talks/wonderful-world-apis.html): A tour of the wide world of web APIs.
- [Crons, Queues, and Daemons. Oh my!](https://timlytle.net/talks/crons-queues-daemons-oh-my.html): When to use a cron, when to use a queue, and when you really need a daemon.
